modern: Let us try to persuade men. But act even against their will, when the principles of justice lead that way. If, however, any man stands in your way by using force, turn to contentment and tranquillity, and at the same time use the obstacle for the exercise of some other virtue; and remember that your attempt was made conditionally, that you did not want to do the impossible. What, then, did you want?—Some such effort as this.—But you achieve your aim, even if the things you were moved towards are not accomplished.
original: Let us try to persuade them [men]. But act even against their will, when the principles of justice lead that way. If however any man by using force stands in thy way, betake thyself to contentment and tranquillity, and at the same time employ the hindrance towards the exercise of some other virtue; and remember that thy attempt was with a reservation [conditionally], that thou didst not desire to do impossibilities. What then didst thou desire?—Some such effort as this.—But thou attainest thy object, if the things to which thou wast moved are [not] accomplished.

explained.summary:
Try to persuade people, but act even without their agreement when justice demands it. If someone blocks you by force, accept it calmly and use the obstacle to practise a different virtue, like patience. Remember that you always aimed with a reservation, never expecting to do the impossible.

So what did you actually want? To make the right effort. And you’ve done that, even if the outcome didn’t happen.
explained.today: You argued for a change at work and were overruled. You did the part that was yours, which was making the case well. Now the task is accepting the decision gracefully, and perhaps showing patience with the people who disagreed.
